newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek cash rates idle after PM's speech.
newsitem.headline: Greek cash rates idle after PM's speech.

text.p: Greek money rates and forex forwards were fluctuating narrowly in early dealings, unaffected by Prime Minister Costas Simitis's economic policy speech in parliament on Thursday night, dealers said.
"There is little trading activity so far and rates are holding Thursday afternoon levels," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
"Simitis's speech was dull, general and therefore no factor today. The 1997 budget will reveal the government's real intentions," he said. The budget must be presented by the end of November.
The dealer said the markets would react negatively if the 1997 budget deficit was to be slashed to about 4.2 percent of GDP by employing accounting gimmicks rather than healthy spending cuts.
Simitis vowed in his first major economic policy speech to put the country into the EMU by the year 2000, fight tax evasion, cut expenditures and abolish tax breaks for the wealthy.
Other dealers said liquidity would be boosted by about 20 to 25 billion drachmas, the equivalent of Wednesday's forex inflows at the central bank's fixing.
"There is no factor that would justify a major interest rate readjustment today," a trader at a state bank said. "I expect the central bank to drain overnight money at 12.40 percent."
The mark was quoted at 157.00/05 drachmas from Wednesday's 156.990 fix, the dollar at 240.38/43 drachmas from 240.300 and the Ecu at 300.54/64 from 300.450 drachmas.
